title: Resilience simulations for region cutover and GPU throttle
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and execute a suite of resilience simulations that validate SLO behavior, circuit breaker effectiveness, and load-shedding policies across a partial region cutover and progressive GPU pool throttle. Goal: ensure graceful degradation and accurate error-budget accounting when a primary region loses data-plane capacity while control plane and DNS remain reachable, and when GPU pools experience soft exhaustion from long-lived KV/cache-heavy requests.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can reproduce: (a) region data-plane blackhole with control-plane intact, (b) GPU pool soft-exhaustion causing elevated queue depths and tail latency, (c) dependency blackholes for our Vector DB and Auth service.
Circuit breakers trip and fallbacks (model variant or region) activate within configured SLO thresholds and documented rollback conditions.
Load-shedding policy reduces head-of-line blocking and stabilizes p95/p99 tail latencies without violating customer-facing rate limits more than allowed by the error budget policy.
Runbook sections updated with measured thresholds and operator playbooks; dashboards capture error-budget burn and fallback success rate.
Findings and remediation actions assigned with owners and timelines; any P0 regressions have hotfix plans.
No test should require changes to production data; all fault injection is reversible and gated behind feature flags/maintenance windows.
test_plan: Phase 1 - Canary harness: run small-scale synthetic traffic (10% of baseline) to validate injection hooks and metrics collection.

Phase 2 - Region cutover simulation: emulate data-plane blackhole in region-1 by applying iptables blackhole and simulated GPU pool unavailability; leave control-plane VPC routes intact to mimic DNS and control signals passing.

Phase 3 - Progressive GPU throttle: schedule a fleet of long-attention synthetic requests that pin KV cache entries to force pool worker saturation; ramp from 20% to 120% of pool capacity over 30 minutes.
Phase 4 - Dependency blackholes: introduce artificial timeouts for Vector DB and Auth at varying rates (5%, 25%, 50%) and observe cascading effects and circuit-breaker engagements.
Phase 5 - Routing and fallback validation: verify smart-routing moves traffic to region-2 and to quantized/model-variant fallbacks; assert expected latency and cost delta.
Phase 6 - Load-shed effectiveness: exercise token-based and request-priority shedding rules and ensure high-priority tenant traffic preserved per SLA tier.
Phase 7 - Post-mortem collection: capture traces, KV cache hit/miss, kernel-scheduling signals, GPU utilization, request queue lengths, and error-budget burn timeline.
Safety: each phase has an abort condition (p50>target*3, p95>target*2, or >10% unintended user errors) that auto-reverts injections.

notes: 2026-02-21: spike validated injection method that toggles BGP announcements + iptables blackhole in a sandbox VPC. Control-plane remained reachable via transit gateway.

2026-02-26: design review with SRE and Serving runtime. Decided to avoid terminating control-plane control channels to preserve orchestration visibility; this better matches customer-visible partial-region failures.
2026-03-01: implemented GPU throttle by scheduling synthetic long-attention workflows that allocate large KV caches; observed that naive throttling caused head-of-line blocking in the worker queue.
2026-03-04: Miguel implemented a per-worker queue timeout and preemption hook; reduced request tail latency in stage environment by ~35% during throttling tests.
2026-03-08: PM feedback (Jordan Lee): require explicit canary approval UI and automatic Jira ticket generation when the harness triggers an abort; added to scope.
2026-03-11: Security review checklist started; we will gate the harness behind RBAC and an allowlist of test regions and clusters.
observations: Circuit-breaker default thresholds (5xx rate or 50ms queue increase) were too conservative for GPU-exhaustion scenarios; needed a latency-and-queue-based hybrid threshold.
Smart routing fallback to quantized model variants preserved throughput but increased top-line token latency; successful when paired with prefix-KV cache warming.
Dependency blackholes exposed uninstrumented code paths in the retry logic that duplicate requests into the queue — caused transient queue amplification.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Adopt a hybrid circuit-breaker that considers queue depth and kernel busy ratio rather than only error-rate — trades simplicity for better tail protection.
Prefer region failover over local retries for long-tail backend timeouts to avoid amplifying load; this can increase cross-region egress cost but reduces error-budget burn.

Implement progressive load-shedding that protects SLOs for paying tenants: shed best-effort and free-tier requests earlier, preserve enterprise routes; this is a customer-experience tradeoff that must be documented.
Do not enable destructive fault injection in production automatically; require a manual two-person signoff and maintenance-window gating for production runs.
